subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should OpenClaw ship a public after-compaction resetSession API, and if so, is its permanent contract reason-only or must it preserve the unshipped explicit-session-key overload?
rationale: This creates a compatibility-sensitive plugin API and special bundled-harness plumbing; repository history does not establish the earlier explicit-key proposal as a shipped contract, so automation cannot choose the permanent surface.

options.title: Ship reason-only API
options.body: Expose only resetSession("new" | "reset") on reset-capable after-compaction contexts and remove the explicit-key overload as unshipped compatibility baggage.

options.title: Preserve explicit-key compatibility
options.body: Keep the explicit-key overload with maintainer-approved documentation, a named deprecation/removal plan, and tests proving it can never target another session.

options.title: Do not add the core API
options.body: Close or redesign the branch around a narrower owner-plugin or lifecycle contract if core hooks should not initiate resets.

recommendation.title: Ship reason-only API
recommendation.body: Expose only resetSession("new" | "reset") on reset-capable after-compaction contexts and remove the explicit-key overload as unshipped compatibility baggage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the compaction hook lifecycle and hook-context contract being extended.
